edits.definition: Contraception is the deliberate prevention of pregnancy by methods that block one step of the reproductive process — the release of the egg, the meeting of sperm and egg, or the implantation of the embryo. The main families are barrier methods (condoms, diaphragms) that physically stop sperm, hormonal methods (pills, implants, injectables) that suppress ovulation, intrauterine devices such as the copper-T that prevent pregnancy inside the uterus, surgical methods (vasectomy in males, tubectomy in females) that block the passages permanently, and natural methods such as withdrawal and the rhythm method. Barrier methods alone additionally protect against sexually transmitted diseases.

Sexual reproduction is the mode of reproduction in which a new organism arises from the fusion of two specialised cells — the male and female gametes — to form a single cell, the zygote. Because the zygote carries genetic material from both parents, the offspring are not identical copies but show variation in their traits. The process requires gamete formation and fertilisation, and the variations it generates provide the raw material on which natural selection acts, helping a species survive changing conditions.

Asexual reproduction is the mode of reproduction in which a single parent gives rise to offspring without the formation or fusion of gametes. The new individuals arise by ordinary mitotic cell divisions, so they are genetically identical to the parent and to one another — clones. The principal modes are binary fission in Amoeba and bacteria, multiple fission in the malarial parasite Plasmodium, budding in yeast and Hydra, fragmentation in Spirogyra, regeneration in Planaria and Hydra, and spore formation in the bread mould Rhizopus. The strategy trades variety for speed and certainty.

Fossils are the preserved remains, impressions or traces of organisms that lived in the remote past, found mainly in sedimentary rock. A fossil forms when an organism is buried quickly under mud or silt, shielding it from decay; over long ages the layers harden into rock while minerals may replace or fill the body's structures, or the buried form may leave a cast or an empty mould. Because deeper sedimentary layers were laid down earlier, fossils from lower strata are older than those above them, which makes fossils dated evidence of evolutionary history — including transitional forms such as Archaeopteryx, which carries features of both reptiles and birds.

Life processes are the basic functions that all living organisms perform continuously to keep themselves alive — nutrition, which supplies energy and raw materials; respiration, which releases energy from food; transportation, which carries water, food and gases between the parts of the body; and excretion, which removes the harmful metabolic wastes produced inside the cells. Together these processes maintain the stable internal conditions that cellular activity requires. In unicellular organisms all four take place by simple diffusion across the single cell surface, while larger organisms need specialised tissues and organ systems to carry them out.

Classification is the systematic arrangement of living organisms into groups on the basis of shared characteristics and evolutionary relationships. It makes the enormous diversity of life studyable by placing related organisms together, gives every organism a universally accepted name and position, reveals evolutionary links through shared features, and helps in identifying species that are useful or harmful to humans. Sound classification rests on fundamental traits — such as cell structure, body symmetry and level of body organisation — before finer ones, so that the groups reflect real relationships rather than superficial resemblance.
